dedupe_keys.name: household environmental health survey around the deonar dumping ground mumbai december 2025

description: This small survey asks households living beside Mumbai's Deonar dumping ground, one of India's largest open dumps, about their exposure to smoke, odour and dust and the illnesses they report. The producer is Mohammed Shadab Shah of Karmaveer Bhaorao Patil College, who ran structured interviews with KoboToolbox. Coverage is 100 households in three zones at different distances from the site in Shivaji Nagar, interviewed between 21 and 30 December 2025. Each record gives the zone, household size, years of residence, whether members work with waste, tobacco use, perceived exposure, and self-reported respiratory, digestive and skin symptoms and tuberculosis history; names, coordinates and other identifiers were removed. The anonymised table is available as a free download from Zenodo under the Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 licence. Caveats: a small sample, self-reported health, one winter fortnight, no measured pollution and no control area far from the site. Simulation uses: setting exposure and health burden assumptions for communities near landfills and dump fires, and weighing health gains from closing or capping dumps. Related records: the EDF landfill methane map (data-edf-landfill-methane-map) and GHGSat landfill plumes (data-ghgsat-landfill-methane-plumes) describe emissions from large disposal sites.
